answers.who: young people and the general public who will be living in the world in 2076, and want a say in how climate and governance tradeoffs are decided
answers.broken: online debates about letting AI run decisions are loud and one-sided, with everyone having opinions but no one showing the actual odds or consequences of different choices
answers.changed: a tool that gives an AI (or a person) a fixed budget of 360 points across six levers to allocate, then simulates thousands of possible futures to 2076, showing best case, most likely, and worst case outcomes with visual pins for disasters and breakthroughs
answers.proof: the AI's own allocation kept 92% of simulated futures below 2 degrees but led to 31 million people displaced by sea rise in the most likely future; Claude's version kept 26% below 2 degrees with 18 million displaced; the test audience's human-chosen allocation only displaced 8 million but kept 0% of futures below 2 degrees
